newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa opposition assess challenge to ruling ANC.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa opposition assess challenge to ruling ANC.

text.p: Leaders of South Africa's newest opposition movement met liberal Democratic Party (DP) legislators on Wednesday to probe the potential for a united stand against the domination of the African National Congress.

Former National Party chief negotiator Roelf Meyer and axed ANC politician Bantu Holomisa, who was sacked as a deputy minister in President Nelson Mandela's government last year, met DP leader Tony Leon at a Johannesburg hotel.
Leon, whose party won 2.5 percent of the vote in the country's first democratic elections in 1994, told reporters that a merger was not out of the question.

"We're talking about the options that are available to the three of us and in what ways we can cooperate. All three of us believe that the move towards a one-party state in our country needs to be arrested as soon as possible.
"Nothing is impossible but it is probably very premature to talk about mergers, acquisitions or anything of that sort," said Leon.
Meyer said the talks were exploratory and a conclusion was unlikely on Wednesday.
"Our common interest is South Africa and the question is how best we can make a contribution towards improving the quality of life of all South Africans," he said.
Holomisa, who was sacked by the ANC for accusing a cabinet minister of taking bribes during apartheid rule, said he hoped to overcome the country's race divisions.

"We need a (political) home for many people in South Africa. We hope that for the first time we will move away from racial connotations in South Africa and have a party that represents all population groups," he said.
Leon and Holomisa said it was unlikely that either of them would initiate talks with former president F.W. de Klerk's National Party (NP), which built and then disbanded apartheid.
"The National Party has argued with history for too long. It's sell-by date has expired," said Leon.
The NP has suffered a rash of defections to Meyer, including 10 members of the Pretoria City Council, since their falling out earlier this year.
Municipal councillors can cross the floor but members of provincial and national parliaments cannot defect without losing their seats.
Meyer and Holomisa plan to launch their opposition party on September 27 to lobby for voter support ahead of the 1999 polls.
